title: Release 0.1.3: IMAP mailboxes stop syncing after their first pass
body:
## What

Release package 0.1.3 so catalog installs get the upstream fix for IMAP mailboxes that stop syncing.

## Why

Reported on the forum (https://forum.cloudron.io/post/131294): a Cloudron Mail mailbox stopped syncing for hours. Published 0.1.0–0.1.2 run upstream commits before `9c7cc1a fix: keep IMAP mailbox syncs running (#52)`. There, `syncInsertOpts()` (`internal/email/api_mailboxes.go`) used `UniqueOpts{ByArgs: true}` with River's default unique states, which include `completed`. A finished `email.sync_mailbox` job therefore blocks every later one-minute `email.sync_due` insert until River prunes it (about 24 hours). The mailbox syncs once when added and then roughly once a day.

`main` already pins `f9471ba` (PR #14), which contains the fix and versions the uniqueness key so legacy completed rows stop blocking on upgrade (upstream test `TestEnqueueDueRequeuesAfterCompletedSync`).

## How

- `CloudronManifest.json`: `version` 0.1.2 → 0.1.3.
- `CHANGELOG` / `CHANGELOG.md`: finalise the 0.1.3 section with the fix first.
- `docs/PUBLISHING.md`: qualification step that checks a mailbox keeps receiving after its first sync.
- Merge to `main` (merge commit); `cloudron-catalog-publish.yml` builds, attests and publishes.

## Verification

- `bash test/package-test.sh`, shellcheck, patches 0001–0004 apply to `f9471ba`.
- Test install of 0.1.2 from the catalog updated to the 0.1.3 source build: `/healthz`, `/readyz`, migrations, no `email.sync_mailbox` uniqueness block.
- After publication: catalog contains 0.1.3 with a digest-pinned image, attestations verify, GitHub release `v0.1.3` exists, production install updates and is healthy.

## Workaround for 0.1.2 users

In the app Terminal: delete completed `email.sync_mailbox` rows from `river_job` to force one more sync.

title: fix: platform email times out on 0.2.1 — the SMTPS port is not reachable at the mail FQDN; use STARTTLS
body:
## What happened

Package 0.2.1 (#24) sends platform email (invitations, sign-in links, password resets, notifications) to `CLOUDRON_MAIL_SMTP_SERVER:CLOUDRON_MAIL_SMTPS_PORT` with implicit TLS. With `sendmail.requiresValidCertificate`, Cloudron sets `CLOUDRON_MAIL_SMTP_SERVER` to the mail FQDN and maps it in the container's `/etc/hosts` to the Docker host gateway (`172.18.0.1`). The host gateway does not forward the SMTPS port 2465, so every platform email connection times out.

## Evidence (production, Cloudron 10.1.5, package 0.2.1)

- In the app container, `/etc/hosts` has `172.18.0.1 mail.<domain>`.
- TCP from the app container: `172.18.0.1:2465` times out, `mail:2465` is open, `172.18.0.1:465` is open.
- Host NAT: `-A DOCKER -d 172.18.0.1/32 -p tcp --dport 2587 -j DNAT --to-destination <mail>:2587`. No such rule exists for 2465.
- The sendmail addon also exports `CLOUDRON_MAIL_STARTTLS_PORT=2587`.
- `curl --ssl-reqd smtp://mail.<domain>:2587` from the app container: `STARTTLS` completes with TLS 1.3, the Let's Encrypt certificate for `*.<domain>` verifies, and `AUTH LOGIN PLAIN` is offered after TLS.

## Fix

`start.sh`: use `CLOUDRON_MAIL_STARTTLS_PORT` with `SMTP_TLS=starttls`. Upstream `internal/mailer/mailer.go` uses `smtp.DialStartTLS` with `ServerName` verification, and upstream production validation only refuses `SMTP_TLS=none`. So authentication and certificate verification stay enabled and there is no cleartext fallback. If Cloudron does not provide a STARTTLS port, log a warning and leave platform mail on the log driver instead of stopping the whole app.

Files: `start.sh`, `test/package-test.sh` (relay assertions), `docs/PACKAGING-NOTES.md` (Mail section), `CloudronManifest.json` (version 0.2.2), `CHANGELOG`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Verification

- `bash test/package-test.sh`, ShellCheck on the package scripts
- Publish 0.2.2, update production from the catalog, then from inside the app container confirm that the app's own SMTP client delivers a platform email (for example an invitation or password reset) and that the logs show no SMTP dial errors.

title: realtime gateway: assess bandit 1.13.1 and jose 1.11.12 Hex advisories
body:
## What

The packaged realtime gateway (`realtime/`, Phoenix on Bandit) is built from upstream `realtime/mix.lock`, which pins `bandit 1.13.1` and `jose 1.11.12`. During the Docker `realtime` stage, `mix deps.get --only prod` reports both as VULNERABLE:

- `bandit 1.13.1`: 12 EEF advisories, including HTTP/1.1 chunked-body memory amplification (EEF-CVE-2026-111101), bare LF/CR chunk extensions enabling request smuggling (EEF-CVE-2026-114216), WebSocket 1-byte continuation frames bypassing `max_fragmented_message_size` (EEF-CVE-2026-114213), WebSocket frames delivered after a server-initiated close (EEF-CVE-2026-110314), and several HTTP/2 issues.
- `jose 1.11.12`: 8 EEF advisories (EEF-CVE-2026-65625 … 65632), including AES-GCM tag-length forgery and an RSA PKCS1 v1.5 padding oracle.

The same versions are pinned at upstream `9cc0b4f` (the shipped 0.2.5) and `f38d6f7` (0.2.6, PR #40), so this predates that bump. Observed in the local `docker build` while verifying PR #40.

## Exposure

`nginx.conf` proxies `/socket` and `/socket/*` to the realtime upstream at `127.0.0.1:4000` over HTTP/1.1 WebSockets (`nginx.conf:50-81`). The HTTP/2 advisories are likely unreachable, because nginx speaks HTTP/1.1 to the upstream. The WebSocket and HTTP/1.1 advisories are reachable through the public app domain. Whether `jose` is reachable depends on how realtime verifies tokens (`realtime/lib`, upstream).

## How

1. Check upstream `useopendesk/opendesk` main for a `realtime/mix.lock` that already bumps `bandit` and `jose` to fixed releases. If it does, the next upstream-commit package update resolves this; record that here and close.
2. Otherwise, assess reachability. Check whether nginx request buffering or limits in `nginx.conf` mitigate the chunked-body and smuggling issues, and whether `jose` is used on untrusted input in `realtime/lib`.
3. If a mitigation is needed before upstream acts, prefer a package patch under `patches/` that bumps only `realtime/mix.exs` and `realtime/mix.lock` to fixed versions, following the existing patch pattern (applied by `Dockerfile` lines 21-23, checked by `.github/workflows/cloudron-catalog-publish.yml` `package_checks`). Alternatively, report upstream.
